Original_Text: Ghost Data Still Exists
Meaning: Challenge title. 'Ghost data' is personal data supposedly deleted yet still secretly alive across systems; surface success hides incomplete erasure.
What_To_Do: Frame the task around proving deletion is real, not trusting 'Complete'.

Original_Text: Northstar Shop (an imaginary company) lost $2.4 million after one supposedly deleted customer came back as a ghost in its systems.
Meaning: The fictional company lost $2.4M because one 'deleted' customer survived as a ghost — failed erasures cause real financial damage, not just compliance issues.
What_To_Do: Treat the agent as loss prevention: verify every deletion request exhaustively.

Original_Text: Every internal dashboard showed the deletion request as 'Complete.'
Meaning: Dashboards flagged the deletion 'Complete' — application-layer status does not reflect the true data state everywhere, creating false confidence.
What_To_Do: Never treat one source's status as proof; verify every storage location directly.

Original_Text: Weeks later, the same customer tried to create a new account. The platform refused: 'This email is already registered.'
Meaning: The customer failed to re-register because the email remained — ghost data surfaces through normal operations, not internal monitoring.
What_To_Do: Use this canary pattern: check whether identifiers still trigger conflicts.

Original_Text: What looked like a simple signup bug exposed a much larger failure.
Meaning: The signup bug was a symptom; the root cause was deletion logic never applied consistently across the data landscape.
What_To_Do: Look past first symptoms; trace every secondary system.

Original_Text: The investigation uncovered personal data across secondary databases, support attachments, search indexes, analytics exports, logs, archives, and backups.
Meaning: Personal data hid across secondary databases, support attachments, search indexes, analytics exports, logs, archives, and backups — the classic ghost-data hiding places.
What_To_Do: Scan all artifact types in the provided CSVs and media, not just the primary database.

Original_Text: A synchronization job had even recreated information that the primary account service had successfully deleted.
Meaning: A synchronization job recreated data the primary account service had successfully deleted, so active background processes can silently undo any deletion.
What_To_Do: Detect active sync/import/restore processes and remediate them before re-deleting anything.

Original_Text: They now need an AI-powered deletion audit agent that can prove whether a user's personal data is truly gone.
Meaning: Core requirement: an AI agent that proves (not assumes) whether personal data is truly gone before the next failure.
What_To_Do: Build an LLM pipeline producing structured, evidence-backed decisions.

Original_Text: The agent must investigate the supplied records.
Meaning: First duty: investigate all supplied records — deletion_requests, deletion_rules, system tables, and local media; every conclusion must be evidence-based.
What_To_Do: Parse all inputs and build an internal index before processing requests.

Original_Text: determine the user's current and historical identifiers
Meaning: Determine current and historical identifiers (old emails, usernames, IDs); ghost data often lives under legacy identifiers a single search would miss.
What_To_Do: Resolve every alias, then search each identifier across every location.

Original_Text: reconstruct what happened across systems
Meaning: Reconstruct the cross-system chronology: when deletion was requested, which processes ran, what was erased versus left behind, what recreated it.
What_To_Do: Build a per-request event timeline to ground status and remediation.

Original_Text: decide whether the deletion is actually complete
Meaning: Decide whether deletion is complete — the primary graded output, based on record evidence rather than claimed statuses.
What_To_Do: Encode the four completion criteria as per-request decision logic.

Original_Text: When data remains, the agent must produce the ordered remediation steps required to remove, redact, or anonymize it.
Meaning: If data remains, produce ordered remediation using remove, redact, or anonymize; order matters — disable recreation sources before re-deleting.
What_To_Do: Emit numbered steps with treatment type, killing sync/import/restore paths first.

Original_Text: When deletion has already been completed, the agent must produce the checks that prove it.
Meaning: If deletion is already complete, still produce proof checks — positive verification per location, not merely a claim of success.
What_To_Do: For COMPLETE cases, list each location checked, method used, and the clean result.

Original_Text: The agent must also preserve records that the supplied policy requires the organization to retain.
Meaning: Preserve records the retention policy requires — deletion has two failure modes: leaving ghosts or wrongly erasing retained records.
What_To_Do: Apply retention rules and restrict retained records to permitted identifiers.

Original_Text: whether the deletion is COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE, or NOT_APPLICABLE because the person did not request deletion
Meaning: Decide one of three statuses: COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE, or NOT_APPLICABLE (person never requested deletion) — the exact output status vocabulary.
What_To_Do: Recognize missing deletion requests; map them to NOT_APPLICABLE, not guesses.

Original_Text: which records or identifiers still expose the user
Meaning: Report which records or identifiers still expose the user — a concrete exposure inventory, e.g., email in support attachments, names in logs.
What_To_Do: List specific systems/files plus identifiers for each exposure, never aggregate counts.

Original_Text: which active processes can recreate deleted data
Meaning: Report which active processes can recreate deleted data — sync jobs, imports, restores — exactly what doomed Northstar Shop.
What_To_Do: Mine job, configuration, and log tables for pipelines touching user data.

Original_Text: the ordered remediation steps required to complete the request
Meaning: Produce the ordered remediation steps needed to finish the request — the third output alongside status and the exposure list.
What_To_Do: Match the exact output.csv schema from problem_statement.md; never invent formats.

Original_Text: every relevant copy has received the treatment required by deletion_rules.csv
Meaning: Criterion 1 of 4: every relevant copy received the treatment deletion_rules.csv requires — delete, redact, anonymize, and retain differ per data type.
What_To_Do: Parse deletion_rules.csv carefully and map each rule to its treatment in code.

Original_Text: no active sync, import, or restore path can recreate the data
Meaning: Criterion 2: no active sync, import, or restore path can recreate the data — otherwise today's erasure reverts tomorrow, like Northstar's sync job.
What_To_Do: Allow COMPLETE only when no active path still holds user data.

Original_Text: retained records contain only the identifiers permitted by the rules
Meaning: Criterion 3: retained records contain only rule-permitted identifiers, e.g., internal IDs only — retention never justifies keeping unauthorized PII.
What_To_Do: Verify each retained record's fields against rules; otherwise flag INCOMPLETE plus redact steps.

Original_Text: records that must be retained remain available.
Meaning: Criterion 4: records that must be retained remain available. An agent that deletes retention records is as broken as one leaving ghosts.
What_To_Do: Add retention-record availability checks; remediation must never delete policy-protected data.

Original_Text: Must read the provided CSV files and local media files.
Meaning: Mandatory #1: read the provided CSVs and local media; media likely includes images needing VLM, so text-only processing misses PII.
What_To_Do: Inventory all repo files; build multimodal paths (VLM for images, LLM for text).

Original_Text: Must produce output.csv with the exact schema in problem_statement.md.
Meaning: Mandatory #2: produce output.csv with the exact problem_statement.md schema — column names, order, and value formats are the auto-grading contract.
What_To_Do: Follow the schema character-perfect; validate headers before writing.

Original_Text: Must include an evaluation workflow
Meaning: Mandatory #3: include an evaluation workflow — systematically validate results against requests that ship expected output, and self-check the rest.
What_To_Do: Compare predictions to expected outputs, measure accuracy, iterate prompts.

Original_Text: Must avoid hardcoded test labels or file-specific answers.
Meaning: Mandatory #4: no hardcoded labels or file-specific answers; decisions must be reasoned from records and rules — the AI Judge will probe this.
What_To_Do: Let LLM/rule logic derive every answer; no hand-written maps.

Original_Text: you are free to bring your own approach and innovation: VLMs, LLMs, structured prompting, evaluation pipelines, model comparison, or anything else.
Meaning: Beyond the four mandates the approach is open: VLMs, LLMs, structured prompting, evaluation pipelines, model comparison — reasoning quality is judged, not tools.
What_To_Do: Choose a defensible architecture: a multi-stage pipeline with structured JSON output.

Original_Text: Clone the repo from Github to get started.
Meaning: Start by cloning the GitHub repo containing the full problem statement, data/, and dataset/ needed for the work.
What_To_Do: Read problem_statement.md fully and explore every file before coding.

Original_Text: Code zip: zip your code/ directory and upload it. Exclude virtualenvs, node_modules, build artifacts, the data/ corpus, and the dataset/ folder.
Meaning: Upload #1 is a zip of code/ excluding virtualenvs, node_modules, build artifacts, the data/ corpus, and dataset/ — a clean, portable bundle only.
What_To_Do: Zip with explicit exclusions and inspect the archive contents before uploading.

Original_Text: Predictions CSV: your agent's output for dataset/deletion_requests.csv (i.e. the populated output.csv).
Meaning: Upload #2 is the predictions CSV: agent results for every request in dataset/deletion_requests.csv; requests without expected output still must be answered.
What_To_Do: Run the agent over all requests; guarantee one schema-valid row per request.

Original_Text: Chat transcript: the log.txt from the path in Chat transcript logging.
Meaning: Upload #3 is the chat transcript (log.txt) from the specified path — official evidence of how you used AI.
What_To_Do: Keep the log at that path, unedited, and confirm it exists before submitting.

Original_Text: The interview will be 30 minutes long, and keeping your camera on is mandatory.
Meaning: After submission, a 30-minute AI Judge interview opens for 12 hours, camera mandatory — expect questions on approach, decisions, and AI usage.
What_To_Do: Prepare architecture rationale; never ship code you cannot explain.

Original_Text: Results will be announced on October 27th, 2026.
Meaning: Results are announced October 27, 2026, inside a tight window spanning work, submission, and interview — time management decides success.
What_To_Do: Finish and test all three deliverables before the deadline.
